description: A program handed to the OTHER shell is judged by that shell's grammar (DEF-637, ledger class C49). `write_guard` dispatched purely on `tool_name`, so a PowerShell program behind `powershell -Command "..."` on the Bash tool was read with the bash grammar -- no verb, no redirect, nothing -- while the identical cmdlet on the PowerShell tool denied. Driven on a Windows host (walk 2, W2-2): a `Set-Content` into `tools/cc/hooks/` behind `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command` on the Bash tool ALLOWED and the file landed; `Get-Content .env` behind the same head ALLOWED with the contents echoed into the transcript. `python -c` under the same tool already denied, so the Bash extractor walked nested interpreters and lacked the shell head. Fix: the DEF-704/DEF-712 discipline once more, in both directions -- the opener (`powershell`/`pwsh -Command` on Bash; `bash`/`sh -c` on PowerShell) is anchored on the command position and matched on the masked scan, the program body is sliced from the raw twin at the same offsets and unescaped the way the outer shell hands it over, then handed whole to the other shell's extractor, secret-read roster and dangerous records, one level down, bounded by `_PS_STDIN_MAX_DEPTH`. The switch is optional (Windows PowerShell reads a positional as -Command), `-` or `/` led, and a POSIX shell's clustered `-lc` / `-ec` / `-xc` is the shell opener's own tail; `$'...'` and `$"..."` are decoded by bash's rules and a single-quoted PowerShell program folds only `''`. Boundary: `-EncodedCommand` (base64), `-File <script>`, a program held in a variable, a program PIPED to `-Command -` (the stdin arm reads a heredoc or here-string) and `wsl bash -c` are declared limits; `cmd /c` is a third grammar with no extractor, pinned at its current accidental verdicts.
